unbiased_ranking_raw_eeg.description: Rank 60 candidate face latents for a hidden mental target from 3000 unlabeled stimulus/EEG pairs per session, using the windowed raw-EEG representation (29 channels x 7 windows = 203 features). Stimuli and candidates are drawn independently of the target, so only the EEG/stimulus pairing carries information about the target. Paper analogue: Table 1 (EEG windowing).

score_distance_pearson_r.description: Mean over sessions of the Pearson correlation between a solver's candidate scores and the candidates' true distances to the hidden target (constant scores count as 0). Lower is better: higher scores should go to nearer candidates.

target_rank.description: Mean rank of the hidden target among the 60 candidates (1 = best), expected value under uniformly random tie-breaking.

top_rank_distance.description: Mean latent distance from the top-scored candidate to the hidden target (ties at the top averaged). The paper's preferred, perceptually grounded metric.

target_top1_accuracy.description: Fraction of sessions in which the hidden target is ranked first (expected under random tie-breaking).

target_top5_accuracy.description: Fraction of sessions in which the hidden target is within the top five (expected under random tie-breaking).

reciprocal_target_rank.description: Mean reciprocal rank of the hidden target (expected under random tie-breaking).

near_target_top_rank_rate.description: Fraction of sessions whose top-scored candidate lies within latent distance 5.0 of the hidden target (ties at the top averaged).

unbiased_ranking_raw_eeg._note: Setup changed from the paper's: the paper's simulation places every stimulus at a recorded distance around the target and every candidate at a uniform distance from it, so stimulus and candidate geometry alone reveal the answer (a no-EEG centroid ranking is perfect on that protocol, see redteam/hardening/results/paper_protocol_check.json). The gym draws stimuli and candidates from one target-independent, homogeneous distribution (uniform on a 2-sphere of radius 17.3 in a random 3-D subspace of the 512-D latent space; expected target-candidate distance 23.07 vs the paper's random baseline 23.08), assigns each stimulus a recorded EEG row at the nearest recorded distance, and scores 48 hidden sessions per experiment. The paper's numbers are therefore not on this setup's scale and are kept under _paper_results; `results` holds the gym reference run (CURSOR-LR and the paper's S-LR / Dummy controls) on the hidden test.

_paper_results.source: Table 1 / Appendix Table 2 (EEG windowing), Table 3 (top-k), N = 9234, target-centred synthetic stimuli, uniform-distance candidates
